symptom: ako/mxcli#1913 (mendixlabs/mxcli#1720): `validation feedback $Entity2/Error message 'not good';` failed check with "missing MESSAGE at ''not good''" for an attribute named Error (any case) — exactly what describe writes for such an attribute, so describe output for the microflow did not re-parse; quoting it (`$Entity2/"Error"`) worked.
cause: ERROR_MESSAGE is one compound lexer token (`E R R O R WS+ M E S S A G E`, for the `error message` clause). The lexer has no context, so the member name and the MESSAGE keyword after it were swallowed into it and the path ended at `$Entity2/`.
file: mdl/grammar/MDLLexer.g4 (right-edge predicate {!p.followsMemberSeparator()}? on the grouped ERROR_MESSAGE alternatives, helper in @lexer::members reading TokenStartCharIndex); cmd/gen-completions/main.go (firstAlternative strips the group's opening paren, else ERROR MESSAGE dropped out of lsp_completions_gen.go)
insight: A multi-word lexer token is a keyword collision that no keyword list shows: `Error` and `message` are each fine as names, only the pair collides, so lexesAsBareIdentifier/mdlIdent cannot see it and quoting in describe would not have helped an unquoted script. Fixing it in the lexer, not the one parser rule, covers every position an attribute path can take. Two traps in the predicate: skipping line breaks backwards lets a line comment ending in '.' or '/' (`-- see the docs.`) read as a separator and break the clause on the next line, and a block comment's closing `*/` ends in a slash — both are controls in the test, and the newline-skipping draft failed them. `$` inside an @lexer::members comment is an ANTLR attribute reference (error 128), and gen-completions reconstructs a multi-line rule from its first line, so a grouped `( E R R O R …` must have its paren stripped there. **A lexer predicate goes on the right edge**: the first version put it on the left edge, which ANTLR evaluates at every token start, disabling the lexer DFA cache — `check` over 300 example scripts went from 43 s to 91 s and the conformance and upgrade corpus tests hit the 30-minute timeout, while every unit test passed. On the right edge it runs only after `error message` matched (42 s vs 44 s, noise); the token start then comes from TokenStartCharIndex, since LA(j<0) is relative to the current index. Time a lexer change against a control binary, not just its tests. Proven by stubbing the predicate to false (the reported 'missing MESSAGE' returns in the visitor and describe round-trip tests) and by a control-binary sweep of all 1210 .mdl files in the repo: identical results.
